text: A firm in a monopolistically competitive market is producing the profit maximizing quantity at 60 units of output at a price of 12 per unit. What is the firm’s economic profit if the firm’s average variable cost is 8, its marginal cost is 7,and its average fixed cost is 2 at 60 units of output?
explanation: Economic profit is total revenue minus total cost, so the firm earns $12 times 60, or $720, in revenue and pays an average total cost of $8 plus $2, or $10, times 60, or $600, in costs. Subtracting cost from revenue gives a profit of $120. A common wrong step is to subtract only total variable cost from revenue and get $240, but fixed costs must be included to calculate economic profit.

unit: Market Failure & the Role of Government

text: Which of the following is an example of a negative externality in production?

options.A: An electronics store decreases the price of TVs during the holidays.
options.B: A car insurance company charges a higher price for teenage drivers.
options.C: A local paper mill emits an odor imposing equilibrium costs on nearby residents.
options.D: A pine tree in a public park provides pleasant shade for residents.
options.E: A photographer accepts e price for work below marginal cost.

unit: Market Failure & the Role of Government
explanation: A negative externality in production occurs when a firm’s manufacturing process imposes costs on third parties who are not involved in the market transaction. The paper mill’s odor forces nearby residents to bear unwanted costs from production, which matches this definition perfectly. Option B may seem appealing because it involves higher costs for a risky population, but it is merely an insurance company pricing policies according to private risk rather than shifting costs onto outside bystanders.

text: If the government imposes a binding price ceiling in the gasoline market, which of the following will occur in the short run?

options.A: The demand for gasoline will increase
options.B: The demand for gasoline will decrease
options.C: The quantity demanded of gasoline will increase
options.D: All individuals in the gasoline market will be better off
options.E: All individuals in the gasoline market will be worse off

explanation: A binding price ceiling set below equilibrium lowers the price consumers pay, causing a movement along the demand curve that increases the quantity demanded while decreasing the quantity supplied and creating a shortage. Because this is a change in price rather than a shift in consumer preferences, the demand for gasoline itself does not increase or decrease. It is also incorrect to say that everyone is worse off, since the consumers who are able to purchase gasoline at the lower price are better off.

text: The market for bottled mineral water is perfectly competitive. After she discovery of several new sources of mineral water, the price of bottled mineral water decreases. The substitution effect of the price decrease implies an increase in which of the following?

text: Nikita was working at a law firm earning an annual salary of 80,000, but she decided to start her own business. She used a building she owns and had been renting to a tenant for 15.000 a year. explanation: Economic profit subtracts both explicit and implicit opportunity costs from total revenue. Nikita’s implicit costs include the $80,000 salary and the $15,000 rental income she gave up, totaling $95,000. text: Which of the following is true about the market supply curve for a good?

options.A: It is derived from the summation of the marginal revenue product of labor hired by individual firms
options.B: It is derived from the summation of the marginal product of labor hired by individual firms
options.C: it is derived from the summation of individual firms, quantity supplied at each price
options.D: It lies above the market demand curve at quantities less than the market equilibrium quantity
options.E: It lies below the market demand curve at quantities greater than the market equilibrium quantity

explanation: The market supply curve is created by horizontally summing the quantity that each individual firm is willing to supply at every possible price. This simply means adding up all firms’ output decisions at each price level to find total market supply. Option B might confuse you because firms use labor to produce goods, but summing the marginal product of labor across firms does not give the market supply curve; marginal product measures how much output an additional worker produces, not how much output firms plan to sell at various prices.
